name: Juray
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Panigrahi, Subhashish (depositor). 2026. Juray language documentation. ELAR deposit SO_0cd58401-696e-4f30-bf2d-f21309527dc8 (OpenSpeaks Archives).
sources.note: Two interview videos (juray001/002.mp4) with subtitles, recorded 2019 for the documentary MarginalizedAadhaar; no grammar sketch, phonology notes or wordlist.

sources.citation: Horo, Luke & Gregory D. S. Anderson. 2021. Towards a prosodic typology of Kherwarian Munda languages: Santali of Assam. Papers from SEALS 30 (JSEALS Special Publication), 298-317.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Table 2 'Munda language prominence patterns' (the text layer) has a Sora row -- 'Second syllable in disyllables (Horo 2017); Duration, Intensity, Fundamental Frequency' -- and a Gorum row; no Juray row (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S. & Opino Gomango. 2017 [conf. 2016]. On the current status and state of Juray in the Sora-Juray cluster. In N. Ostler & P. Mohanty (eds.), Language Colonization and Endangerment: long-term effects, echoes and reactions (FEL XX, Hyderabad 9-12 Dec 2016), 103-109. Hungerford: FEL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. The abstract says 'All aspects of Juray structure, its lexicon, phonology and morphosyntax are showing effects of language contact', but the body treats only sociolinguistics, lexical correspondences (Sora /i/ ~ Juray /u/ < Proto-Sora-Juray *ɨ, sec. 4), person indexing, case, capabilitive and plural marking; a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|prosod|syllab|tone in pp. 103-109 yields no prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Horo, Luke. 2017. Phonetic description of Assam Sora. PhD thesis, Dept. of Humanities and Social Sciences, IIT Guwahati (TH-1980).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Prominence data are for Assam Sora only. On Juray (the text layer): Anderson & Harrison 'claim that although Juray is often regarded as a separate South Munda language, it may actually be a divergent Sora dialect'; Assam Sora speakers 'do not consider Juray to be a separate language'; 'Juray speakers of Assam are not recorded in this dissertation'. No Juray stress statement.

sources.citation: Anand, R. Selvin. 2002. Savara. In Linguistic Survey of India, Special Studies: Orissa. Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India (Census of India). Sketch in the Austro-Asiatic section.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent: the Savara sketch's phonology and morphophonemics sections (deletion, syllable-loss, glottal-stop changes) contain no stress, accent or intonation statement. Relevant to identity only: 'the Savaras who speak Imani, Jura and Jadu varieties of Savara language are often called as Lanjia Savaras' (line 26398) -- 'Jura' = Juray-sor.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid jura1242; Wikipedia 'Juray language'; Living Tongues Institute Munda publications list (livingtongues.org/munda-languages-publications/) and Sora project page.
sources.note: No stress information. Glottolog cites Anderson 2007 and Anderson 2020: 159-160 for subclassification; Wikipedia cites Anderson (ed.) 2008 and Bapuji et al. 2025; Living Tongues gives the CORE link to the FEL XX proceedings used above and says 'possibly Juray should be considered an ethnically distinct dialect of Sora'.

sources.citation: Bapuji, Mendem, Opino Gamango & P. Phani Krishna. 2025. Juray: An Endangered Variety of the Sora Group of Lects. In N. S. Dash, S. Arulmozi & N. Ramesh (eds.), Handbook on Endangered South Asian and Southeast Asian Languages, 173-209. Springer.
